problem.description: dh-audit of A15–A16 found an ambiguous Faraday-law exercise condition.
symptoms: A16 originally asked what happens when the field rotates to 90 degrees, but a field rotating during the observation can itself induce emf even if its final angle to the loop normal is 90 degrees

investigation.root_cause: The exercise conflated a fixed 90-degree field orientation with the transient rotation process; the derivative of flux must include changes in both field magnitude and angle.

tests_run.command: primary-source comparison with OpenStax University Physics 2 §13.1
tests_run.output: Faraday emf is negative time derivative of flux; orientation changes can induce emf
A15 electric-field and A16 fixed-angle magnetic examples match independent numeric calculations
75 pages, 890 references, no broken local targets
No page overflow; figure regions preserve native 760/900px widths and scroll

changes: Specified that the 90-degree field direction is fixed while only its magnitude changes
Explained that emf may arise during the rotation and that zero flux at a final instant alone does not imply zero emf
resolution.remaining: Ideal uniform-field model only; no FEM, PCB EMC measurement, physical part validation or reviewer sign-off is claimed.
